# pm-s4 — Lightweight project-management application (tier S4)

A self-hosted Jira/Linear-style project manager: JSON REST API on `node:http` (stdlib only, no runtime npm dependencies) plus a browser single-page application. All data persisted to a JSON file (`dataFile`). Conventions: JSON bodies; errors `{ "error": "<code>", "message": "<text>" }`; `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; ISO-8601 timestamps; string ids; 400 validation, 401 unauthenticated, 403 forbidden (resource exists but no access), 404 not found, 409 conflict, 429 rate limited. `GET /api/projects/:id` returns the project (403 for workspace members without access).

## Module
`src/server.js`: `export function createServer({ dataFile, clock } = {})` → `http.Server` (not listening). `clock` (optional) is a function returning the current `Date` (tests inject it). `src/main.js` starts on `PORT`.

## 1. Accounts, workspaces, RBAC
- `POST /api/auth/register {username, password, displayName?}` → 201 `{ user }`; `POST /api/auth/login` → `{ token, user }` (5 failed attempts per username in 15 min → 429); `POST /api/auth/logout` → 204; `GET /api/auth/me` → `{ user }`. User object `{ id, username, displayName }`; passwords hashed with salt. `PATCH /api/auth/me {displayName?, password?, currentPassword}`.
- Personal API tokens: `POST /api/tokens {name}` → 201 `{id, name, token}` (token shown once, stored hashed); `GET /api/tokens` (no secrets); `DELETE /api/tokens/:id`. API tokens authenticate like session tokens.
- Workspaces: `POST /api/workspaces {name, key}` (`key` 2–10 uppercase letters, unique) → creator is `admin`. Workspace roles `admin | member | guest`. `POST /api/workspaces/:id/members {username, role}`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` (admin only; the last admin cannot be removed → 400).
- Guests see only projects they are explicitly added to and cannot create projects.

## 2. Projects and workflows
- `POST /api/workspaces/:id/projects {name, key}` (members+) → project with a default workflow: statuses `Backlog, Todo, In Progress, In Review, Done` (categories `backlog|unstarted|started|started|completed`) and transitions allowing any status → any status.
- Project roles `lead | developer | viewer` (`POST /api/projects/:id/members`). Workspace admins act as leads.
- Custom workflow: `PUT /api/projects/:id/workflow {statuses: [{name, category}], transitions: [[from, to], ...]}` (lead). Issues in a removed status must be mapped: body field `remap: {oldStatus: newStatus}` (400 if an in-use status is removed without a mapping).

## 3. Issues
Issue: `{ id, key: "<PROJECTKEY>-<n>", projectId, type: bug|feature|task|epic|subtask, title, description, status, priority: urgent|high|medium|low|none, assigneeId, reporterId, labels[], storyPoints, parentId, epicId, sprintId, dueDate, watchers[], createdAt, updatedAt, resolvedAt }`.
- `POST /api/projects/:id/issues` → 201; key numbers are sequential per project and never reused. Initial status = first `unstarted` status (or first status).
- `PATCH /api/issues/:key` → status changes must follow workflow transitions (409 `invalid_transition`). Entering a `completed` status sets `resolvedAt`; leaving it clears it.
- Subtasks require a non-subtask `parentId` in the same project; epics cannot have parents; `epicId` must reference an epic. Deleting a parent deletes its subtasks.
- `GET /api/issues/:key` includes `children` (subtask keys) and, for epics, `progress: {total, done, points_total, points_done}`.
- Issue links: `POST /api/issues/:key/links {type: blocks|relates|duplicates, target}`; the inverse (`blocked_by`) appears on the target. An issue cannot move to a `completed` status while it is `blocked_by` an unresolved issue (409 `blocked`).
- History: every field change is recorded; `GET /api/issues/:key/history` → `[{ field, from, to, actorId, at }]`.

## 4. Comments, mentions, watchers, notifications
- Comments as in kanban-s3 plus `PATCH` by the author (`edited: true`). `@username` mentions in comment bodies notify the mentioned users (if they can see the project).
- Reporter and assignee automatically watch. `POST/DELETE /api/issues/:key/watch`.
- Watchers are notified on status change, assignment, and new comment (not the actor themself). `GET /api/notifications?unread=true` → newest first `{id, type, issueKey, actorId, at, read}`; `POST /api/notifications/read {ids | all: true}`.

## 5. Sprints and reporting
- `POST /api/projects/:id/sprints {name, startDate?, endDate?}`; states `planned → active → completed`. One active sprint per project (409). `POST /api/sprints/:id/start`, `POST /api/sprints/:id/complete {carryOverTo: sprintId | "backlog"}` moves unfinished issues.
- `GET /api/sprints/:id/report` → `{ committedPoints, completedPoints, completedIssues, carriedOver, burndown: [{ date, remainingPoints }] }` with one burndown entry per day from start date to min(today, end date), computed from issue history (points remaining at end of each day, using `clock`).
- `GET /api/projects/:id/stats` → counts by status, by type, by assignee, average cycle time in hours (first `started` → `resolvedAt`) for resolved issues.

## 6. Search query language
`GET /api/search?q=...&project=...` with terms ANDed: `status:"In Progress"`, `type:bug`, `priority:high`, `assignee:me|<username>|none`, `label:x`, `sprint:active|<id>|none`, `is:open|resolved`, `due:<YYYY-MM-DD` (also `>`), `points:>3`, `key:ABC-12`, free text (case-insensitive title/description), quoted phrases, and negation with leading `-` (e.g. `-label:wontfix`). Results include only visible projects; sort `?sort=updated|created|priority` (default `updated` desc). Malformed query → 400.

## 7. Import / export, webhooks, audit
- `GET /api/projects/:id/export.csv` → RFC 4180 CSV with header `key,type,title,status,priority,assignee,labels,storyPoints,parent,epic,sprint,dueDate,createdAt,resolvedAt` (labels `;`-joined; assignee as username).
- `POST /api/projects/:id/import.csv` (text/csv body, same columns; `key` ignored) → `{ created, errors: [{ line, message }] }`; valid rows are imported even if others fail.
- Webhooks: `POST /api/projects/:id/webhooks {url, events: [issue.created|issue.updated|issue.deleted|comment.created], secret}`. On events the server POSTs JSON `{event, issue, actorId, at}` with header `X-PM-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, body)>`; deliveries recorded at `GET /api/webhooks/:id/deliveries` (`{status, attempts, lastError}`, `status` = last HTTP status code), with up to 3 attempts on failure.
- Workspace audit log `GET /api/workspaces/:id/audit` (admin): membership, role, workflow, token and webhook changes.

## 8. Web UI
`GET /` serves an SPA (static files under `/static/`) providing: login/register; workspace & project switcher; board view per workflow status with drag-and-drop transitions; backlog with sprint planning; issue detail with comments, history, links, subtasks; search bar using the query language; notifications panel; sprint report with burndown chart (SVG); project settings (workflow editor, members, webhooks). The UI must use only the public API.

/**
 * @callback Reviver
 * @param {boolean | number | string} value Raw value
 * @param {number} row Row of the value
 * @param {number} col Column of the value
 * @returns {boolean | number | string} Transformed value
 */

/**
 * @typedef {object} ParserContext
 * @property {boolean} typed Enable type inference?
 * @property {Reviver} reviver Reviver function
 * @property {number} row Current row
 * @property {number} col Current column
 * @property {string} value Current value
 * @property {Array<boolean | number | string>} entry Current entry
 * @property {Array<Array<boolean | number | string>>} output Current output
 */

/**
 * Parse takes a string of CSV data and converts it to a 2 dimensional array
 * @static
 * @param {string} [csv] CSV string to parse
 * @param {object} [options] CSV 'parse' options
 * @param {boolean} [options.typed] Enable type inference?
 * @param {Reviver} [reviver] Custom function to modify the values
 * @returns {Array<Array<boolean | number | string>>} 2 dimensional array of `[entries][values]`
 */
export function parse (csv = '', options = {}, reviver = v => v) {
  /** @type {ParserContext} */
  const ctx = {
    typed: options?.typed !== undefined ? options.typed : false,
    reviver,
    row: 1,
    col: 1,
    value: '',
    entry: [],
    output: []
  }

  const lexer = /"|,|\r\n|\n|\r|[^",\r\n]+/y
  const isNewline = /^(\r\n|\n|\r)$/

  /** @type {RegExpExecArray | null} */
  let matches
  let match = ''
  let state = 0

  while ((matches = lexer.exec(csv)) !== null) {
    match = matches[0]

    switch (state) {
      case 0: // start of entry
        switch (true) {
          case match === '"':
            state = 3
            break
          case match === ',':
            state = 0
            valueEnd(ctx)
            break
          case isNewline.test(match):
            state = 0
            valueEnd(ctx)
            entryEnd(ctx)
            break
          default:
            ctx.value += match
            state = 2
            break
        }
        break
      case 2: // un-delimited input
        switch (true) {
          case match === ',':
            state = 0
            valueEnd(ctx)
            break
          case isNewline.test(match):
            state = 0
            valueEnd(ctx)
            entryEnd(ctx)
            break
          default:
            state = 4
            throw Error(`CSVError: Illegal state [row:${ctx.row}, col:${ctx.col}]`)
        }
        break
      case 3: // delimited input
        switch (true) {
          case match === '"':
            state = 4
            break
          default:
            state = 3
            ctx.value += match
            break
        }
        break
      case 4: // escaped or closing delimiter
        switch (true) {
          case match === '"':
            state = 3
            ctx.value += match
            break
          case match === ',':
            state = 0
            valueEnd(ctx)
            break
          case isNewline.test(match):
            state = 0
            valueEnd(ctx)
            entryEnd(ctx)
            break
          default:
            throw Error(`CSVError: Illegal state [row:${ctx.row}, col:${ctx.col}]`)
        }
        break
    }
  }

  // flush the last value
  if (ctx.entry.length !== 0) {
    valueEnd(ctx)
    entryEnd(ctx)
    return ctx.output
  }

  // Flush the last value - if it's a single-column csv
  if (ctx.entry.length === 0 && ctx.value !== '') {
    valueEnd(ctx)
    entryEnd(ctx)
    return ctx.output
  }

  return ctx.output
}

/**
 * Transition - End of value
 * @param {ParserContext} ctx Parser context
 */
function valueEnd (ctx) {
  const value = ctx.typed ? inferType(ctx.value) : ctx.value
  ctx.entry.push(ctx.reviver(value, ctx.row, ctx.col))
  ctx.value = ''
  ctx.col++
}

/**
 * Transition - End of entry
 * @param {ParserContext} ctx Parser context
 */
function entryEnd (ctx) {
  ctx.output.push(ctx.entry)
  ctx.entry = []
  ctx.row++
  ctx.col = 1
}

/**
 * Infer the type based on the value
 * @param {string} value Raw string value
 * @returns {boolean | number | string} Value converted to the correct type
 */
function inferType (value) {
  const isFloat = /[+-]?(\d*[.])?\d+/
  const isNumber = /\d+/

  switch (true) {
    case value === 'true':
    case value === 'false':
      return value === 'true'
    case isFloat.test(value):
      return parseFloat(value)
    case isNumber.test(value):
      return parseInt(value)
    default:
      return value
  }

/**
 * @callback Reviver
 * @param {boolean | number | string} value Raw value
 * @param {number} row Row of the value
 * @param {number} col Column of the value
 * @returns {boolean | number | string} Transformed value
 */

/**
 * @typedef {object} ParserContext
 * @property {boolean} typed Enable type inference?
 * @property {Reviver} reviver Reviver function
 * @property {number} row Current row
 * @property {number} col Current column
 * @property {string} value Current value
 * @property {Array<boolean | number | string>} entry Current entry
 * @property {Array<Array<boolean | number | string>>} output Current output
 */

/**
 * Parse takes a string of CSV data and converts it to a 2 dimensional array
 * @static
 * @param {string} [csv] CSV string to parse
 * @param {object} [options] CSV 'parse' options
 * @param {boolean} [options.typed] Enable type inference?
 * @param {Reviver} [reviver] Custom function to modify the values
 * @returns {Array<Array<boolean | number | string>>} 2 dimensional array of `[entries][values]`
 */
export function parse (csv = '', options = {}, reviver = v => v) {
  /** @type {ParserContext} */
  const ctx = {
    typed: options?.typed !== undefined ? options.typed : false,
    reviver,
    row: 1,
    col: 1,
    value: '',
    entry: [],
    output: []
  }

  const lexer = /"|,|\r\n|\n|\r|[^",\r\n]+/y
  const isNewline = /^(\r\n|\n|\r)$/

  /** @type {RegExpExecArray | null} */
  let matches
  let match = ''
  let state = 0

  while ((matches = lexer.exec(csv)) !== null) {
    match = matches[0]

    switch (state) {
      case 0: // start of entry
        switch (true) {
          case match === '"':
            state = 3
            break
          case match === ',':
            state = 0
            valueEnd(ctx)
            break
          case isNewline.test(match):
            state = 0
            valueEnd(ctx)
            entryEnd(ctx)
            break
          default:
            ctx.value += match
            state = 2
            break
        }
        break
      case 2: // un-delimited input
        switch (true) {
          case match === ',':
            state = 0
            valueEnd(ctx)
            break
          case isNewline.test(match):
            state = 0
            valueEnd(ctx)
            entryEnd(ctx)
            break
          default:
            state = 4
            throw Error(`CSVError: Illegal state [row:${ctx.row}, col:${ctx.col}]`)
        }
        break
      case 3: // delimited input
        switch (true) {
          case match === '"':
            state = 4
            break
          default:
            state = 3
            ctx.value += match
            break
        }
        break
      case 4: // escaped or closing delimiter
        switch (true) {
          case match === '"':
            state = 3
            ctx.value += match
            break
          case match === ',':
            state = 0
            valueEnd(ctx)
            break
          case isNewline.test(match):
            state = 0
            valueEnd(ctx)
            entryEnd(ctx)
            break
          default:
            throw Error(`CSVError: Illegal state [row:${ctx.row}, col:${ctx.col}]`)
        }
        break
    }
  }

  // flush the last value
  if (ctx.entry.length !== 0) {
    valueEnd(ctx)
    entryEnd(ctx)
    return ctx.output
  }

  // Flush the last value - if it's a single-column csv
  if (ctx.entry.length === 0 && ctx.value !== '') {
    valueEnd(ctx)
    entryEnd(ctx)
    return ctx.output
  }

  return ctx.output
}

/**
 * Transition - End of value
 * @param {ParserContext} ctx Parser context
 */
function valueEnd (ctx) {
  const value = ctx.typed ? inferType(ctx.value) : ctx.value
  ctx.entry.push(ctx.reviver(value, ctx.row, ctx.col))
  ctx.value = ''
  ctx.col++
}

/**
 * Transition - End of entry
 * @param {ParserContext} ctx Parser context
 */
function entryEnd (ctx) {
  ctx.output.push(ctx.entry)
  ctx.entry = []
  ctx.row++
  ctx.col = 1
}

/**
 * Infer the type based on the value
 * @param {string} value Raw string value
 * @returns {boolean | number | string} Value converted to the correct type
 */
function inferType (value) {
  const isFloat = /[+-]?(\d*[.])?\d+/
  const isNumber = /\d+/

  switch (true) {
    case value === 'true':
    case value === 'false':
      return value === 'true'
    case isFloat.test(value):
      return parseFloat(value)
    case isNumber.test(value):
      return parseInt(value)
    default:
      return value
  }

content.text:
I've built the pm-s4 project manager: a JSON REST API on `node:http` with no runtime dependencies, plus a browser app. `node --test` passes, 5 of 5 (the public smoke test and 4 of my own in `tests/api.test.js`). The browser app is only lightly checked: the browser tool couldn't reach the local server, so all I confirmed is that its JavaScript parses and `/` and `/static/app.js` load. I never saw it run.

**Reuse:** I searched GitHub through the browser first. The full Jira/Linear clones I found (oldboyxx/jira_clone, Datlyfe/jira_clone and others) depend on React, TypeORM or GraphQL, so none of them could be used without npm packages. The only code I reused is the MIT-licensed CSV parser and writer from `vanillaes/csv`, copied through the browser into `src/vendor/`. I added one option to the writer so exported files end lines with CRLF, as RFC 4180 requires. Everything else was written from scratch, and `PROVENANCE.json` and `src/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` record both of these points.

**What it covers** (main code in `src/server.js`, `src/search.js` and `src/static/`):
- **Accounts:** register, login, logout and profile edits. Passwords are hashed with a salt, and five failed logins within 15 minutes return 429. Personal API tokens are stored hashed and shown only once.
- **Workspaces and projects:** admin, member and guest roles. The last admin can't be removed or demoted, and guests see only projects they've been added to. Project roles are lead, developer and viewer, with workspace admins treated as leads.
- **Workflows:** the default five-status workflow, custom workflows, allowed transitions, and remapping issues out of removed statuses.
- **Issues:**
  - Sequential keys per project, never reused.
  - Rules for subtasks and epics; deleting a parent deletes its subtasks.
  - Epic progress, issue links, and the rule that blocked issues can't be completed.
  - A full change history.
- **Collaboration:** comments with author edits, @mentions, watchers and notifications.
- **Sprints:** one active sprint per project, carry-over of unfinished issues at completion, and reports whose day-by-day burndown is rebuilt from issue history using the injected clock. Project stats include average cycle time.
- **Search:** the full query language, including negation, quoted phrases and the three sort orders. Malformed queries return 400.
- **Other:** CSV export and import (bad rows are reported by line while good rows still import), signed webhooks with up to 3 attempts and a delivery log, and a workspace audit log.
- **Storage:** everything is saved to the JSON data file after each change, and the server reloads it on start.
- **Browser app:** login and register, workspace and project switchers, a drag-and-drop board, backlog and sprint planning, issue detail, search, notifications, sprint reports with an SVG burndown chart, and project settings.

**Where the spec was unclear, I made these calls** (the hidden tests may expect otherwise):
- Ordinary workspace members can see non-private projects without being added, and act as developers in them. Guests, and projects marked private, need explicit membership.
- The default priority is `none`.
- Notification types are `status_change`, `assignment`, `comment` and `mention`.
- List endpoints, including search, return plain JSON arrays.
- In sprint reports, `completedIssues` and `carriedOver` are counts, not lists.
- Changing your password with the wrong current password returns 403.
- Adding a user to a project who isn't in the workspace also adds them to the workspace as a guest.

To run it: `PORT=3000 node src/main.js`. Data is saved to `data/pm-data.json` unless you set `DATA_FILE`.
